chunks: He said: Abul Qasim, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qawlawayh, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from his father, who reported from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idrees together, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from al-Husayn ibn Nasr ibn Muzahim al-Attar, from his father, from Amru ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, peace be upon him, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdillah ibn Haraam al-Ansari saying:

If Salman and Abu Dharr, may Allah have mercy on them both, were to divulge to these people who claim devotion to you, O Ahlul Bayt, they would say: These two are liars. And if these claimants were to see those two, they would say: They are insane.

key_terms.الدُّمُوع: Tears — a sign of spiritual tenderness and fear of Allah
key_terms.اللَّاحِقِين: Those who follow/join — refers to all mortals who inevitably follow the dead
key_terms.الْبَطَّالُون: The idle ones — those who waste their time in heedless amusement
key_terms.الْخُشُوع: Humility/Khushu‘ — deep reverence and submissiveness before God
key_terms.مَوْعِظَة: Admonition/lesson — moral instruction drawn from reflection
key_terms.مِيل الْحُزْن: The kohl-stick of sorrow — a metaphor for adorning the eyes with grief rather than cosmetics

ai.seo_question: What did Allah reveal to Prophet Isa (Jesus) about weeping, humility, and visiting graves?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) relates a divine revelation (wahy) from Allah to Prophet ‘Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, peace be upon him), commanding him to weep, show humility, and reflect upon death by visiting graves. The exhortation contrasts the heedless laughter of the idle with the sober contemplation of mortality, urging ‘Isa to draw admonition from the deceased and acknowledge his own inevitable death. This type of divine counsel to earlier prophets was commonly cited in Shi‘a tradition to emphasize universal ethical principles — particularly humility, sorrow for the hereafter, and remembrance of death.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 5. He said: Abul Qasim, Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Qawlawayh - may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from his father, who reported from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idrees together, from ‘Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn Sa’d al-Ashariy, from al-Husayn ibn Nasr ibn Muzahim al-Attar, from his father, from Amru ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Jo’afi, from Abu Ja’far al-Baqir, peace be upon him, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdillah ibn Haraam al-Ansari say:

’If Salman and Abu Dharr, may Allah bless them with mercy, were to divulge (the excellence of Ahlul Bayt) to these people who claim to be the partisans of Ahlul Bayt, they would say: "These two are liars." And if these were to see them, they would say: "These are insane."
